arguments.explanation: To find portfolios with only bonds, I first identify portfolios that have at least one holding. Then, I filter for those where all holdings are of type 'Bond'. I do this by grouping by portfolio_name and checking that the count of 'Stock' assets is 0 and the count of 'Bond' assets is greater than 0.

FROM portfolios p
JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type = 'Stock' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type = 'Bond' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY p.portfolio_name ASC;

result.sql:

FROM portfolios p
JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.asset_type = 'Stock' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
